summary: Lists errors found since the publication of the RFCs for version 1.0 of the Internet Open Trading Protocol and gives corrections for them. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This is a list of mistakes spotted in the instructions for an online-shopping protocol, along with the fixes.

subtitle: Corrections to the Internet Open Trading Protocol version 1.0 specification.

tldr.problem: Since publication of the IOTP v1.0 specification (which included RFC 2801, the largest RFC ever issued at the time), implementers and reviewers discovered errors in the document definitions and protocol descriptions.
tldr.mechanism: This errata document identifies specific errors in the IOTP specification, including Document Type Definition (DTD) attribute type swaps, XML syntax errors, and incomplete enumeration lists in the protocol specification.
tldr.outcome: Implementers of IOTP are provided with corrections to ensure interoperability and correct understanding of the protocol's structure and requirements.

today: RFC 3504 is an Informational errata document. While IOTP never achieved widespread adoption and the protocol is now historic, the errata remain relevant for anyone implementing or studying the original IOTP v1.0 specification.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Internet Open Trading Protocol (IOTP) Version 1.0 specifies a framework for Internet commerce transactions between consumers and businesses. IOTP allows different parts of the transaction (such as payment processing and order fulfillment) to be distributed among different service providers, and it does not require a prior relationship between buyer and seller.

Since publication of the three RFCs defining IOTP v1.0 (RFCs 2801, 2802, and 2803), several errors have been identified in the specification, particularly in the largest RFC (RFC 2801). This errata document lists these errors and provides corrections.
sections.plainLanguage: IOTP is a protocol for buying things online. The original instructions had mistakes, and this document explains what was wrong and how to fix it.

sections.title: DTD and XML Definition Errors
sections.content:
The PackagedContent element in the IOTP XML definition had its attribute types swapped. The incorrect definition assigned CDATA type to the Content attribute and NMTOKEN type to the Name attribute. The corrected version should assign NMTOKEN type to Name and CDATA type to Content, with Transform remaining as (NONE|BASE64) defaulting to NONE.

The Attribute element had an XML syntax error in its content specification. The original notation used ( ANY ), which is invalid DTD syntax. The correct syntax is simply ANY without parentheses. The element's type and critical attributes remain as NMTOKEN and enumerated (true|false), both required.
sections.plainLanguage: Two mistakes in the XML recipe: one had the ingredient types backwards, and another had incorrect parentheses syntax.

sections.title: Protocol Semantic Corrections
sections.content:
In the section describing authentication transactions (Section 9.1.13, page 234 of RFC 2801), a word was incorrectly chosen. The text stated that if an authentication transaction succeeds, the original IOTP transaction is restarted. The correct word is continued, reflecting that the transaction resumes from where it was paused for authentication, rather than beginning anew.

The specification of the IOTP Signature Type attribute (Section 7.19.1, page 150) provided an incomplete list of allowed signature message types. The original list included: OfferResponse, PaymentResponse, DeliveryResponse, AuthenticationRequest, AuthenticationResponse, PingReq, and PingResponse. The corrected list adds three additional types: AuthenticationStatus, InquiryRequest, and InquiryResponse. These additional types are also documented in Section 6.1.2 and Section 12.1 of RFC 2801.
sections.plainLanguage: Two mistakes in how the protocol works: one used the wrong word for what happens after authentication, and another forgot to list all the types of messages that need signatures.

sections.title: IOTP Framework Overview
sections.content:
IOTP Version 1.0 provides a payment system-independent framework for consumer-to-business electronic commerce. The protocol enables different business functions (such as payment processing, order fulfillment, and delivery) to be distributed among different service providers or outsourced, without requiring a prior business relationship between the consumer and merchant.

IOTP messages are structured using XML and carried over the internet, typically via HTTP. The protocol defines message types for offers, payments, delivery, authentication, and inquiry operations, each potentially involving different service providers with different cryptographic signatures to authenticate the various parties involved in the transaction.
sections.plainLanguage: IOTP lets an online purchase be handled by different companies: one for payment, one for shipping, one for customer service. They all communicate using signed XML messages.
